heuristic_statement: The historical audit operates on a strict multi-layer epistemic framework: raw historical facts -> semantic interpretations -> truth decisions. Requirement lifecycle (origin, evolution, active survival, or partial/full supersession) and implementation state (implemented, unenforced, partially represented, or missing) are treated as orthogonal dimensions. Historical Git commits, prompts, and nonce run artifacts serve as empirical evidence of requirement provenance, runtime behavior, and supersession; they are never assumed to be the normative goal. The normative implementation target is exclusively determined by what the machine existing today actually executes, orchestrates, and deterministicly validates across its Node.js source, GitHub Actions workflows, configuration files, and persisted schemas. An outstanding defect constitutes present corrective work if and only if the underlying user requirement survives un-superseded and today's executable machine fails to fully enforce it.
decomposition_rationale: To maintain strict context isolation, prevent Gemini input-token quota exhaustion, and enable deterministic sequential execution in the GitHub Node evaluator process, the audit is partitioned into 24 focused subquestions. Each subquestion is assigned a bounded set of archive files strictly at or below the 250,000-byte ceiling. The decomposition separates independent evidence domains: (1) current executable runtime, workflows, configuration, and evaluation contracts; (2) canonical specification text and historical requirement evolution; (3) granular empirical nonce execution records covering all 16 nonce runs; (4) cross-cutting requirement lifecycle and supersession synthesis; and (5) exhaustive reconciliation between the current machine and surviving active requirements to isolate genuine corrective gaps.

completeness_strategy: Run-level completeness: Ensure all 16 distinct nonce runs in the archive manifest are explicitly analyzed. Fifteen runs are assigned directly to dedicated subquestions (SQ09-SQ21) using their contained files (state.json, messages.json, or store.json) that fit strictly within the 250,000-byte ceiling. The remaining run (skill_bootstrap_update_20260930T170700), whose individual files each exceed 250,000 bytes, is audited via SQ22 using the complete live git lineage log and historical commit records.

Requirement-level completeness: Extract every historical instruction, prompt directive, and architectural pivot from live-supervisor-lineage.log, git-log.txt, and historical-audit-data.json into a unified requirement registry in SQ23. Trace each requirement through subsequent commits to identify superseding events (both full and partial) or ongoing active status.

Orthogonal lifecycle and implementation separation: Maintain independent tracking for requirement lifecycle (active vs superseded) and implementation state (implemented vs unimplemented). Superseded requirements are classified as non-corrective history, whereas active requirements that lack executable enforcement in send-to-gemini.js or workflows are flagged as present corrective work.

Deterministic verification of current machine: Never infer executable behavior from descriptive documentation (e.g. Agents.md, SKILL.md, or commit self-reports). Ground current behavior strictly in parsed JavaScript logic in send-to-gemini.js, GitHub Actions execution steps in gemini-chat.yml, and schema validation structures in SQ01-SQ05.

Three-layer audit trail: For every requirement and machine feature, document the dependency chain: raw facts (exact code lines, commit SHAs, file excerpts) -> semantic interpretations (inferred author intent, scope, and behavioral meaning) -> truth decisions (active surviving vs superseded, enforced vs corrective gap).

Subquestion reconciliation: Systematically cross-check findings across sub-evaluators in SQ24 to identify contradictions, corroborate behavioral claims against multiple runs, and document any indeterminate or ambiguous requirement boundaries.
